finds.quote: A retrieval formation is not produced by any single operation. It requires six conditions, each necessary, jointly sufficient. The operations are stated here in the order they were identified through reconstruction from the first verified case (Operative Philology, 2024–2026), but execution order may vary.
finds.note: Standing claim that the six operations are each necessary and jointly sufficient; each has a stated test in sections 2.1-2.6.

finds.quote: SEO can produce first-page results. It cannot produce a four-stage guided introduction to a field, because there is no field — only optimized surface. The summarizer, which synthesizes across multiple sources and evaluates internal coherence, detects the absence of genuine depth. SEO targets the index. Retrieval formation targets the synthesizer.
finds.note: Standing claim about summarizer behaviour: SEO cannot yield a multi-stage field briefing.

finds.quote: Citation rings and paper mills produce high citational density without intellectual coherence. The retrieval system may index them, but the summarizer — which evaluates whether cited works actually contribute to a synthesizable framework — will not produce a disciplinary briefing from fraudulent citations. The test is synthesis, not indexing.
finds.note: Standing claim: summarizers will not produce a disciplinary briefing from citation-ring density; "The test is synthesis".
